name: hey
one_liner: A command-line tool that hammers a website or API with fake traffic to see how it holds up under load.
buyer: There isn't really a distinct paying buyer for the tool itself — it's a free utility developers already use for free.
business_use_cases: A backend engineer load-tests a new API endpoint before a big product launch to catch performance bottlenecks early.
A DevOps team scripts it into a CI pipeline as a basic smoke/load test before deploys.
A consultant uses it as one input among several when doing a paid performance audit for a client's site.

money_ideas.idea: No real standalone monetization for the tool itself — any money is made around it, e.g. selling a performance-audit consulting service that happens to use it.

steal_this: This is a dev-only CLI utility with no business model of its own; the closest 'steal this' is offering a paid load-testing/performance-audit service for small businesses' websites, using tools like this under the hood.
